name: one-design-mcp

tools.name: compress_images
tools.description: Make images smaller, by quality or to a target file size (e.g. under 500 KB for a form). Keeps each file’s format unless asked; files that already fit are left as they are; PNGs reach a size by reducing colours. Saved next to the originals as name-compressed.ext.

files.description: Image files or folders (a folder means the images in it). ~ is your home folder.

target_kb.description: Largest allowed size in KB. Leave out to compress by quality instead.

quality.description: Quality when not compressing to a size (30–100). For PNG, below 100 reduces colours.

format.description: Output format. "original" keeps each file’s own (HEIC, AVIF and TIFF become JPEG, GIF becomes PNG).

max_edge.description: Scale down so the longest side is at most this many pixels (never enlarged).

allow_resize.description: To a size: may an image be scaled down if even low quality is too big?

output_dir.description: Folder to save results in. Default: next to each original. Originals are never overwritten.

tools.name: resize_images
tools.description: Resize images to a width, a height or both. fit "inside" keeps the whole picture within the box, "cover" fills the box and crops (keeping the interesting part), "contain" fits it whole and pads the rest. Never enlarges unless asked. Social sizes: see the one-design://presets/sizes resource. Saved as name-WIDTHxHEIGHT.ext.

files.description: Image files or folders (a folder means the images in it). ~ is your home folder.

percent.description: Scale by a percentage instead of a size (e.g. 50).

background.description: Padding colour for fit "contain" (hex, or "transparent" for PNG/WebP).

format.description: Output format. "original" keeps each file’s own (HEIC, AVIF and TIFF become JPEG, GIF becomes PNG).

enlarge.description: Allow making images bigger than they are.

output_dir.description: Folder to save results in. Default: next to each original. Originals are never overwritten.

tools.name: make_qr_code
tools.description: QR codes for links or any text, in your colours, as PNG or SVG (default folder: ~/Downloads/one-design), with a preview. Free makes 1 at a time; Pro makes up to 50 in one go. Keep strong contrast between the colours so phones can scan it.

content.description: The link or text to encode.

contents.description: Several links or texts, one code each (Pro: batch).

error_correction.description: Higher survives more damage (and a logo on top) but makes a denser code.

output_path.description: A file (one code) or folder. Default: ~/Downloads/one-design.

tools.name: lock_link
tools.description: Turns any web address into a one.design link that asks for a password before opening it. The address is encrypted here (AES-256-GCM); the result carries it in the link itself, so no server stores it. Anyone with the link and the password can open it.

url.description: The address to protect, e.g. drive.google.com/… (https:// is added if missing).

password.description: The password people will need. It is not stored anywhere.

hint.description: Optional hint shown before the password. Anyone with the link can read it.

tools.name: convert_images
tools.description: Convert images between WebP, JPEG, PNG and AVIF, including iPhone HEIC photos (on a Mac). Choose the quality, optionally shrink big images, and keep or strip metadata. Saved next to the originals with the new extension (never over them). For PDF pages to images use pdf_toolkit with action "to_images".

files.description: Image files or folders (a folder means the images in it). ~ is your home folder.

format.description: Convert to. WebP is usually 25–35% smaller than JPEG at the same quality; PNG is lossless (best for graphics and screenshots); AVIF is smaller still but slower to make.

max_edge.description: Shrink big images so their longer side is at most this many pixels (e.g. 2560, 1920, 1280). Smaller images are left their size.

metadata.description: "strip" removes EXIF, GPS and camera details (the site’s behaviour); "keep" carries them over.

background.description: JPEG only: the colour for transparent areas, hex.

output_dir.description: Folder to save results in. Default: next to each original. Originals are never overwritten.

tools.name: fit_fill
tools.description: Fit the whole photo onto a square, portrait or story canvas without cropping, and fill the space around it with a blurred copy of the photo or a colour (matched to the photo by default). Canvas by name (square, instagram-square, portrait, instagram-portrait, portrait-34, story, landscape, x-post, linkedin, og, link-preview, pinterest, banner, dribbble) or width and height. Saved next to the originals as name-WIDTHxHEIGHT.jpg.

files.description: Image files or folders (a folder means the images in it). ~ is your home folder.

preset.description: Canvas by name: square, instagram-square, portrait, instagram-portrait, portrait-34, story, landscape, x-post, linkedin, og, link-preview, pinterest, banner, dribbble. Ignored when width and height are given.

width.description: Custom canvas width in pixels (with height).

height.description: Custom canvas height in pixels (with width).

fill.description: "blur": a soft, enlarged copy of the photo fills the gaps. "colour": a flat colour.

colour.description: Fill colour for fill "colour": a hex like #c9f26b, or "auto" for a colour matched to each photo (the average round its edges).

blur.description: How soft the blurred fill is, 1 to 10.

darken.description: Darken the blurred fill, in percent.

margin.description: Space around the photo, in percent of the canvas’s shorter side. At 0 it touches the canvas on its longer side.

corner_radius.description: Rounded corners on the photo, in percent of its shorter side.

shadow.description: A soft drop shadow under the photo.

output_dir.description: Folder to save results in. Default: next to each original. Originals are never overwritten.

tools.name: rename_files
tools.description: Rename a set of files (any kind) with one pattern made of text and tokens: {name} the current name, {n} a number counting up ({n:3} for 001), {date} the file’s date as 2026-10-02, {w}x{h} the image size in pixels, {ext} the extension. The extension is always kept at the end. Starts with mode "preview", which only lists old → new and changes nothing; "copy" makes renamed copies in a new folder; "rename" renames in place.

files.description: Files or folders (a folder means the files in it, not subfolders or hidden files), in the order to number them. ~ is your home folder.

pattern.description: The new name without the extension, e.g. "holiday-{n}" or "{date}-{name}".

start.description: The first number, e.g. 51 to carry on from a previous batch.

digits.description: Digits in {n}: 0 adds zeros only as needed (01–12) so files sort in order. {n:3} in the pattern sets it there.

letters.description: "keep": as typed; "lower": lower case; "web": lower case, dashes for spaces and only letters, numbers, dashes and dots.

mode.description: "preview": list the new names, change nothing. "copy": renamed copies in output_dir (default: a new folder named renamed next to the first file). "rename": rename the files where they are; refused if any new name is already taken.

output_dir.description: For mode "copy": the folder for the renamed copies.

tools.name: make_web_image_set
tools.description: Responsive image sizes for a website in one go (WebP and JPEG by default, AVIF or PNG too), into a folder per image, with a ready <picture>/srcset HTML snippet (also saved as snippet.html). Widths larger than an image are skipped, so nothing is enlarged. [Pro tool.]

files.description: Image files or folders (a folder means the images in it). ~ is your home folder.

widths.description: Widths in pixels. Ones wider than the image are left out (the image’s own width is added as the top size instead).

formats.description: Formats to make. The last of JPEG/PNG is the fallback ; WebP and AVIF become lines.

alt.description: Alt text for the . Default: made from the file name.

url_prefix.description: The folder the files will live in on the site, used in the snippet’s paths.

output_dir.description: Where to put the folder of each image. Default: next to the original.

tools.name: slim_svg
tools.description: Make SVG files smaller with SVGO (editor data, comments and metadata out, paths simplified), keeping the viewBox, then render before and after to check they look the same. Saved next to the originals as name-slim.svg; a file that can’t get smaller is left as it is.

files.description: SVG files or folders (a folder means the SVGs in it). ~ is your home folder.

level.description: "safe": removes editor data, comments and metadata, leaves shapes and paths. "balanced": also simplifies paths, merges groups and shortens colours. "max": everything, repeated until nothing more shrinks.

precision.description: Decimal places kept. Small icons can go to 1; detailed illustrations may need 3.

keep_ids.description: Keep IDs (needed if CSS, scripts, sprites or animations refer to parts of the SVG).

remove_size.description: Remove width and height so the SVG scales to its container. The viewBox is always kept.

pretty.description: Indented output for editing by hand. Slightly larger.

output_dir.description: Folder to save results in. Default: next to each original. Originals are never overwritten.

tools.name: multi_crop
tools.description: Crop each image to several sizes at once, keeping the interesting part (or the centre). Sizes by name (square, instagram-square, portrait, instagram-portrait, portrait-34, story, landscape, x-post, linkedin, og, link-preview, pinterest, banner, dribbble), as an aspect ratio like "4:5" (the largest crop of that shape, at the image’s own resolution), or as {name, width, height}. Saved next to the originals as name-<size>.ext. [Pro tool.]

files.description: Image files or folders (a folder means the images in it). ~ is your home folder.

sizes.description: The crops: size names, ratios like "16:9", or {name, width, height}. Default: square, portrait 4:5 and portrait 3:4.

name.description: Short name used in the file name.

crop.description: What each crop keeps: "attention" the most eye-catching part (faces, colour, contrast), "centre" the middle, "entropy" the most detailed part.

format.description: Output format. "original" keeps each file’s own (HEIC, AVIF and TIFF become JPEG).

output_dir.description: Folder to save results in. Default: next to each original. Originals are never overwritten.

tools.name: grid_slide
tools.description: Split one image into an Instagram profile grid, numbered in posting order (post tile 01 first: Instagram shows the newest post top-left, so the bottom-right tile goes first), or into carousel slides that line up seamlessly as people swipe. Presets: ig-row, ig-grid-2, ig-grid-3, ig-grid-4 (3 columns, 3:4 tiles), ig-grid-sq (3×3 square), ig-grid-45 (3×2, 4:5; the default), ig-pano-2, ig-pano-3, ig-pano-5 (4:5 carousels), ig-pano-sq, li-carousel (square), tiktok, story-pano (9:16). Any setting given overrides the preset. Saved in a new folder next to the image. [Pro tool.]

file.description: The image to split. ~ is your home folder.

preset.description: A ready layout (see the description). Default ig-grid-45, or the plain grid/carousel when mode is given.

mode.description: "grid": a profile grid of tiles. "carousel": slides side by side.

shape.description: Each tile or slide’s shape: 1:1 square, 4:5 portrait post, 3:4 (current Instagram profile thumbnails), 9:16 story.

tile_width.description: Width of each tile or slide in pixels; the height follows the shape.

focus_x.description: Which part to keep when the image’s shape doesn’t match: 0 left, 50 centre, 100 right.

output_dir.description: Where to put the folder of tiles. Default: next to the image.

tools.name: make_listing_photos
tools.description: Product photos framed for each marketplace: a near-white border is trimmed, then the product is centred on the marketplace’s canvas at its usual fill. Amazon 2000×2000 (85%), eBay 1600×1600 (80%), Etsy 2000×1600 (75%), Shopify 2048×2048 (80%), Instagram Shop 1080×1350 (75%), Google Shopping 1200×1200 (80%). Works best with products shot on white; the photo’s own background is kept (removing it needs Cutout on one.design). Saved next to the originals as name-<marketplace>.jpg. [Pro tool.]

files.description: Image files or folders (a folder means the images in it). ~ is your home folder.

background.description: "white" (pure white, what most marketplaces want for the main image) or a hex colour.

fill_percent.description: How much of the frame the product fills along its limiting side, the same for every marketplace. Default: each marketplace’s own.

trim.description: Trim the near-white border round the product first.

output_dir.description: Folder to save results in. Default: next to each original. Originals are never overwritten.

tools.name: make_campaign_kit
tools.description: One creative into a matched set of sizes for social posts, stories, link previews and display ads, in one folder. Each size either fills the frame (crop keeping the interesting part) or fits the whole creative over a blurred copy of itself. Sizes: ig-post 1080×1080, ig-portrait 1080×1350, ig-portrait-34 1080×1440, story 1080×1920, x-post 1600×900, dribbble 1600×1200, link 1200×628, youtube 1280×720, li-banner 1584×396, mrec 300×250, leaderboard 728×90, skyscraper 160×600, mobile-banner 320×50. Text layouts (headline, button) are on one.design/campaign-kit. [Pro tool.]

file.description: The photo or key visual. ~ is your home folder.

fit.description: "cover": fill each size, cropping to the most eye-catching part. "fill": the whole creative, with a blurred copy of it filling the space (like fit_fill).

scale.description: 1: exactly each size’s pixels (what ad networks want). 2: double, sharp on high-density screens (a 728×90 banner becomes 1456×180).

name.description: Campaign name for the files, e.g. autumn-launch. Default: the image’s name.

output_dir.description: Where to put the kit folder. Default: next to the image.

tools.name: clean_metadata
tools.description: Remove hidden details from photos before sharing: GPS location, camera, dates, author, XMP edit history, IPTC captions, comments and AI labels / Content Credentials (C2PA). JPEG, PNG and WebP are cleaned losslessly (the picture itself is not re-saved); other formats (HEIC, AVIF, TIFF, GIF) are re-saved without metadata. Reports what each file was hiding. Saved as name-clean.ext next to the original.

files.description: Image files or folders (a folder means the images in it). ~ is your home folder.

keep_rotation.description: Phone photos often store their rotation as metadata. Keeping this one tag (re-written alone) stops them turning sideways. Default true.

keep_colour_profile.description: ICC colour profiles hold no personal data. Removing one can make wide-gamut photos look dull. Default true.

fix_orientation.description: Instead of keeping the rotation tag, turn the pixels upright and re-save (quality 95, not lossless). Only affects photos that have a rotation tag.

output_dir.description: Folder to save results in. Default: next to each original. Originals are never overwritten.

tools.name: redact_images
tools.description: Cover names, emails, card numbers and other private details in screenshots. Give boxes in pixels (or 0–1 fractions of the width and height); the same boxes are applied to every file, for matching screenshots. "marker" (a hand-drawn stroke) and "solid" replace the pixels so nothing can be recovered; "pixelate" and "blur" look softer but short text like numbers can sometimes be guessed, so use marker or solid for card numbers and passwords. The image is re-drawn, so hidden metadata goes too. Saved as name-redacted.ext.

files.description: Image files or folders (a folder means the images in it). ~ is your home folder.

x.description: Left edge (pixels, or 0–1 of the width with units "fraction").

y.description: Top edge (pixels, or 0–1 of the height).

width.description: Box width (pixels, or 0–1 of the width).

height.description: Box height (pixels, or 0–1 of the height).

boxes.description: Areas to cover, measured on the image as it displays (upright).

units.description: "px": boxes in pixels. "fraction": 0–1 of the width and height, which suits screenshots of different sizes.

style.description: marker (the site’s default, a hand-drawn stroke), solid block, pixelate or blur.

format.description: "keep": PNG stays PNG (crisp text), WebP stays WebP, others become JPEG.

output_dir.description: Folder to save results in. Default: next to each original. Originals are never overwritten.

tools.name: pdf_toolkit
tools.description: Work with PDFs on this computer: "merge" (files in order into one), "split" (each page, or ranges like "1-3, 5, 7-" each its own PDF), "extract" (one PDF of chosen pages), "reorder" (a new page order), "rotate" (pages by 90/180/270), "info" (pages, sizes, title, author, producer), "remove_metadata" (clear title, author, subject, keywords, creator, producer, dates and XMP), "to_images" (pages to PNG or JPEG; needs poppler’s pdftoppm installed). Pages are copied as they are, so text stays text. Page numbers start at 1. Saved next to the first PDF (or in output_dir), never over a file.

files.description: PDF files or folders (a folder means the PDFs in it, by name). For merge, in the order given. ~ is your home folder.

pages.description: Pages, like "1-3, 5, 7-" (7- runs to the last page). extract: the pages to keep (required). split: each range becomes its own PDF (leave out to split every page). rotate and to_images: which pages (default all).

order.description: reorder: the new order as page numbers, e.g. [3, 1, 2]. Pages left out of the list are dropped; a page listed twice appears twice.

dpi.description: to_images: resolution (150 suits screens; an A4 page at 150 dpi is 1240×1754 px).

output_dir.description: Folder to save results in. Default: next to the (first) PDF.

tools.name: make_proof_sheet
tools.description: A folder of images into one tidy PDF: a contact sheet (2–6 columns) or one image per page, on A4 or US Letter, with file names under the images and an optional title and date header. Images are embedded as JPEG thumbnails sized to their place on the page, so the file stays small. Saved next to the first image (or where you say) as proof-sheet.pdf or your-title.pdf. [Pro tool.]

files.description: Images or folders, in the order they should appear. ~ is your home folder.

layout.description: "grid": a contact sheet. "single": one image per page.

columns.description: Grid: images across (the site offers 2, 3 or 4; default 3).

page.description: Page size. "fit" (one per page only) matches each image’s shape.

title.description: Optional title at the top of each page (also the file name), e.g. "Client review: round 2".

date.description: Show today’s date in the header.

quality.description: Image detail: print 300 dpi, balanced 200 dpi, email 110 dpi (smallest file).

output_path.description: A .pdf path or a folder. Default: the folder of the first image.

tools.name: check_delivery
tools.description: Check a batch of images against a delivery spec before sending it: formats, file size, exact/min/max width and height, shape (aspect ratio), transparency, colour space, DPI, embedded metadata and file naming. Start from a preset ("web": Website images, "instagram": Instagram feed, "marketplace": Marketplace product photos, "appicon": App Store icon, "print": Print handover (large JPEG/PNG)) or "custom", and override any rule. Reports pass / needs attention / fail per file and which tool fixes each problem. Changes nothing. [Pro tool.]

files.description: Images (and SVGs) or folders. ~ is your home folder.

preset.description: Starting rules. web: JPEG/PNG/WebP/SVG/AVIF under 500 KB, at most 2560 px, lowercase names without spaces. instagram: JPEG/PNG, at least 1080 wide, 1:1, 4:5, 3:4 or 1.91:1, under 8 MB. marketplace: JPEG/PNG, at least 1600×1600, square, no transparency, under 10 MB. appicon: PNG exactly 1024×1024, no transparency. print: JPEG/PNG at least 3000×2000, tidy names. custom: only the rules you give.

max_kb.description: Largest file size in KB (0 = any).

ratios.description: Allowed shapes, like ["1:1", "4:5", "16:9"]. Empty list = any shape.

ratio_tolerance.description: How far off a shape may be, in percent (the site allows 1%).

transparency.description: Transparent areas: any, required (e.g. logos) or forbidden (e.g. app icons, marketplace photos).

colour_space.description: "srgb": flag CMYK, wide-gamut (Display P3, Adobe RGB) and other profiles.

min_dpi.description: Minimum DPI written in the file (0 = any). DPI is only a label; pixel size is what really counts for print.

metadata.description: "none": flag files that still carry EXIF, GPS location, XMP or IPTC.

no_spaces.description: Names without spaces or special characters.

max_name.description: Longest file name in characters (0 = any).

name_pattern.description: A regular expression every file name must match, e.g. "^sku-\d{4}-(front|back)\.jpg$".

tools.name: make_cards
tools.description: Spreadsheet rows into branded social cards, one PNG (or JPEG) per row, using the site’s templates: "poster" (big type on your colour, photo optional), "editorial" (full-bleed photo, white type), "split" (photo plus a colour panel) or "product" (product on a light panel with price and badge). Columns feed the tag, headline, subhead, button (cta) and price, and an image column names each row’s photo file; they are matched by header name unless you map them. Saved in a new folder under ~/Downloads/one-design (or output_dir). [Pro tool.]

csv.description: Path to a .csv or .tsv file with a header row, or the CSV text itself.

template.description: Card design. editorial, split and product need a photo per row.

size.description: Card size: ig-post 1080×1080 (Square), ig-portrait 1080×1350 (Portrait 4:5), ig-portrait-34 1080×1440 (Portrait 3:4), story 1080×1920 (Story / Reel 9:16), x-post 1600×900 (Landscape 16:9), dribbble 1600×1200 (Dribbble shot), link 1200×628 (Link preview), youtube 1280×720 (YouTube thumbnail), li-banner 1584×396 (LinkedIn banner).

columns.description: Which column feeds which part. Unmapped parts are guessed from header names (title, price, photo…).

subhead.description: Column for the smaller line under it.

tag.description: Column for the small label or badge.

image.description: Column holding each row’s photo file name or path.

name.description: Column used for the file names (default: row number).

heading_font.description: Heading font: serif (Instrument Serif), sans (Inter) or mono (JetBrains Mono); this computer’s nearest match if not installed.

logo.description: Optional logo image file (PNG or SVG with transparency works best).

images_dir.description: Folder where the image column’s files are. Default: the CSV’s folder (or your home folder for inline rows).

output_dir.description: Where the new cards folder goes. Default: ~/Downloads/one-design.

tools.name: watermark_images
tools.description: Stamp a text or logo mark on a batch of images, like the site’s Watermark: a tiled diagonal pattern (the default) or a single mark in one of nine positions. Text can be anything, e.g. “© Your Studio 2026”, “Draft”, “Confidential” or “Proof”. Size is a share of each image’s shorter side. Saved next to the originals as name-marked.ext (or into output_dir); originals are never changed.

files.description: Image files or folders (a folder means the images in it). ~ is your home folder.

text.description: The mark’s text, e.g. “© Your Studio 2026”. Default “© One Design”. Ignored when a logo is given.

logo.description: A logo file to use as the mark instead of text (a transparent PNG or an SVG works best).

position.description: Where the mark goes: one of the nine positions for a single mark, or "tiled" for a repeated diagonal pattern over the whole image.

size.description: Mark size as a % of the image’s shorter side (2 to 40). For a logo this sets its longer side (×1.6).

font.description: Typeface for a text mark: serif (Instrument Serif), sans (Inter) or mono (JetBrains Mono), falling back to the computer’s own fonts.

margin.description: Gap from the edge for a single mark, as a % of the shorter side.

angle.description: Tiled pattern rotation in degrees; negative rises to the right.

spacing.description: Gap between tiled marks, as a % of the default gap.

shadow.description: A soft shadow under the mark, so it reads on light and dark areas.

format.description: Output format. "original" keeps each file’s own (HEIC, AVIF and TIFF become JPEG, GIF becomes PNG).

quality.description: Quality for JPEG and WebP (30 to 100).

output_dir.description: Folder to save results in. Default: next to each original. Originals are never overwritten.

tools.name: extract_palette
tools.description: The main colours in an image, like the site’s Palette: HEX, RGB, HSL, how much of the picture each covers, and contrast against white and black, plus CSS variables. Transparent areas are ignored; colours are measured from a downscaled copy, so tiny details may not register. Also saves a swatch card PNG (name-palette.png) in ~/Downloads/one-design.

files.description: Image files or folders (a folder means the images in it). ~ is your home folder.

count.description: How many colours to find (2 to 12). Near-identical ones are merged, so you may get fewer.

order.description: "dominance": most used first. "light": dark to light.

output_dir.description: Folder to save into. Default: ~/Downloads/one-design.

tools.name: make_icon_pack
tools.description: Favicons, app icons and a web manifest from one logo, like the site’s Icon Pack: favicon.ico (16, 32 and 48 px), favicon-16x16.png, favicon-32x32.png, favicon.svg (from an SVG logo), apple-touch-icon.png (180 px), icon-192.png, icon-512.png, icon-512-maskable.png (logo kept inside Android’s safe zone), site.webmanifest and snippet.html with the <head> tags. Saved in a new folder (icon-pack) in ~/Downloads/one-design. Best from an SVG or a PNG of 512 px or more.

logo.description: The logo file: SVG or PNG (512 px or larger), JPEG or WebP.

app_name.description: Name for the web manifest (“My site” if left empty).

short_name.description: Short name under a home screen icon. Default: the name.

padding.description: Space around the logo on the app icons, as a % of the icon.

maskable.description: Include icon-512-maskable.png: Android crops icons to circles or squircles, this keeps the logo inside the safe zone.

logo_colour.description: The logo’s colour in every icon: as it is, or recoloured.

custom_colour.description: Logo colour when logo_colour is "custom", hex like #c9f26b.

favicon_background.description: Behind the tab favicons: "fill" a rounded square in the icon background, "none", or "auto" (a square only for a light logo, which would vanish on light tabs).

adaptive.description: SVG logos only: favicon.svg changes colour to stay visible on light and dark browser tabs.

light_colour.description: Logo colour on light tabs (adaptive), hex like #111111.

dark_colour.description: Logo colour on dark tabs (adaptive), hex like #ffffff.

output_dir.description: Folder to save into. Default: ~/Downloads/one-design.

tools.name: make_logo_package
tools.description: One master logo into a delivery folder, like the site’s Logo Package: a folder per variant (original colours, black, white, black on white, white on black, plus any brand colours you add with their combinations), each with png/ at the widths you choose (transparent unless the variant has a background), jpg/ on a solid background and svg/ when the master is an SVG, and a README.txt of what’s where. Saved as name-logo in ~/Downloads/one-design. Colour variants work best on flat logos. [Pro tool.]

logo.description: The master logo: SVG or a transparent PNG (JPEG and WebP work too).

name.description: Name used in folder and file names. Default: from the file name.

original.description: Include the logo in its own colours.

black_on_white.description: Include black on a white background.

white_on_black.description: Include white on a black background.

colours.description: Extra brand colours (hex); each gets its own one-colour version.

combinations.description: For each extra colour also: on white, on black, white on it and black on it.

widths.description: PNG and JPG widths in px: 256 (avatars, icons), 512 (web), 1024 (slides, docs), 2048 (print, retina), 4096 (large print).

padding.description: Space around the logo on every side, as a % of its longest side.

square.description: Centre the logo on a square canvas (avatars, profile images).

jpg.description: Also export JPGs on a solid background: white behind dark variants, black behind the white one.

svg.description: Include SVGs (only when the master is an SVG). Colour variants use an SVG filter, which some older editors ignore.

output_dir.description: Folder to save into. Default: ~/Downloads/one-design.

tools.name: frame_screenshots
tools.description: Screenshots dressed to share, like the site’s Screen Frame: inside a drawn browser window (title bar with three dots and an address), phone, tablet or laptop, or as a plain rounded card, on a gradient, colour, blurred copy, image or transparent background, at a social canvas size. Devices keep their real screen shape; screenshots are cropped to fill them from the top. Saved next to the originals as name-framed.png (or .jpg). The frames are simple drawings, not any maker’s artwork. [Pro tool.]

files.description: Image files or folders (a folder means the images in it). ~ is your home folder.

frame.description: The frame. "plain" is the screenshot with rounded corners and a shadow, no device.

url.description: Text for the browser’s address bar, e.g. example.com. Empty leaves the bar blank.

tone.description: Frame colour: "dark", "light", or any hex colour for the device.

background.description: Behind the frame: a gradient, one colour, a soft blurred copy of the screenshot, an image, or nothing (transparent PNG).

gradient.description: Built-in gradient: lime, dusk, graphite, paper, sea, peach.

gradient_colours.description: Your own two-colour gradient (hex), top left to bottom right. Overrides "gradient".

background_image.description: Image file for background "image" (cropped to fill).

canvas.description: Canvas: square 2160×2160, portrait 2160×2700 (4:5), portrait-34 2160×2880, story 2160×3840 (9:16), landscape 3840×2160, og 2400×1260 (link preview), dribbble 1600×1200, custom (width × height), or auto (fits the mockup plus padding).

padding.description: Space around the device, as a % of the canvas’s shorter side.

shadow.description: A soft shadow under the device.

style.description: "textured": surfaces lit from the top left. "flat": solid colours, no sheen.

orientation.description: Phone and tablet: upright, on their side, or turned to match each screenshot. A laptop is always landscape.

notch.description: Phone: the camera pill at the top of the screen.

format.description: PNG keeps text in the screenshot crisp; JPEG makes smaller files. A transparent background is always PNG.

output_dir.description: Folder to save results in. Default: next to each original. Originals are never overwritten.

tools.name: make_store_screenshots
tools.description: Store screenshots with a title and your app’s screenshot in a drawn device, like the site’s Store Shots, at the sizes the stores ask for: iOS iPhone 6.9″ 1290×2796 (Apple scales it for every smaller iPhone), iPad 13″ 2064×2752; Android phone 1080×1920, tablet 1440×2560. Up to 10 per device for the App Store, 8 for Google Play. Templates: above (title at the top, device rising from the bottom), below (device above, title underneath), plain (rounded card, no device), tilted, bigtitle (large headline on the left), pair (two devices per slide, two screenshots each), iso (device turned in perspective), full (screenshot fills the image, title over a fade). JPEG (stores reject images with transparency), into a new folder in ~/Downloads/one-design. [Pro tool.]

screenshots.description: Your app’s screenshots in the order they should appear (files or a folder). Each fills the device’s screen, cropped from the top.

platform.description: "ios" for the App Store, "android" for Google Play.

device.description: iPhone or iPad (iOS), phone or tablet (Android).

slides.description: One title (and optional subtitle) per screenshot, in order. Missing ones get placeholder titles, so give one for each.

template.description: Layout: above, below, plain, tilted, bigtitle, pair, iso or full.

background_image.description: An image to fill the background instead of the colour.

font.description: Title font: sans (Inter) or serif (Instrument Serif); subtitles are sans.

device_colour.description: Device colour: "dark", "light", or any hex colour.

output_dir.description: Folder to save into. Default: ~/Downloads/one-design.

tools.name: make_bento
tools.description: Photos, numbers and colour as rounded tiles in one image, like the site’s Bento. Templates and their tiles in reading order (left to right, top to bottom): mosaic-5 (photo (big), photo, text "+38%", photo, photo (big)); hero-2 (photo (big), photo, text "10k"); hero-left-4 (photo (big), photo, text "4.9", colour, photo); three-cols (photo, photo, photo); big-strip (photo (big), photo, text "2026", photo); six-even (photo, photo, photo, photo, photo, photo); stat-board (text "Q3 in numbers", photo, text "2.4M", text "38%", text "120"); feature-3 (photo (big), text "10k", text "98%", text "24/7"); case-cover (text "Case study", photo (big), colour, photo). Give photos to fill the photo tiles in order, and optionally tiles to replace each slot in that same order (a photo, a text tile, or a plain colour); slots you don't replace keep the template’s own. Saved as bento-<template>.png in ~/Downloads/one-design.

template.description: The grid template (see the description for its tiles).

photos.description: Photos for the photo tiles, in order (files or a folder).

tiles.description: Replaces the template’s tiles in reading order: the first entry is the first tile, and so on.

file.description: The photo. Without one, photo tiles take the photos list in order.

focus_x.description: Where the crop sits across, 0 (left) to 100 (right). Default: the most interesting part.

focus_y.description: Where the crop sits down, 0 (top) to 100 (bottom).

title.description: The big line (a headline), or with big_number, a small line under it.

big_number.description: A number or short text set large, e.g. "+38%" or "10k".

caption.description: The small caption at the bottom.

size.description: How big the big line is (it shrinks to fit). Default L.

ink.description: Text colour, hex. Default: white or near black, whichever reads on the fill.

canvas.description: square 1080×1080, portrait 1080×1350, story 1080×1920, landscape 1920×1080, x 1600×900 (X / LinkedIn post), slide 3840×2160, or custom.

padding.description: Space around the grid in px.

text_colour.description: Text colour for every text tile, hex. Default: each tile’s own.

output_dir.description: Folder to save into. Default: ~/Downloads/one-design.

tools.name: make_stamps
tools.description: Turn images into stamps, like the site’s Stamp Maker: "postage" (the picture on paper with perforated edges, a value like “1st” or “£1.50” and a caption), "rubber" (pressed in one ink with a double border, worn edges and a caption) or "seal" (round, inked, with your text around the ring). Rubber stamps and seals print a photo’s tones as an ink dot pattern for a dark or light surface; logos print by their shape. Transparent PNGs up to 1,400 px, saved next to the originals as name-<style>-stamp.png.

files.description: Image files or folders (a folder means the images in it). ~ is your home folder.

caption.description: Postage and rubber: the caption. Seal: the text around the ring.

value.description: Postage: the value in the corner, e.g. “1st” or “£1.50”.

border.description: Postage: a paper margin around the picture with the caption below it. Off, the picture runs to the perforated edge.

ink.description: Rubber and seal ink colour, hex like #c23b2a.

shape.description: Postage and rubber: keep the picture’s proportions, or make the stamp 4:5 portrait or 5:4 landscape (photos cropped, logos fitted whole).

surface.description: Rubber and seal: the surface it’s printed on. Dark prints a photo’s light parts, light prints its dark parts.

tones.description: Rubber and seal: natural reads like the photo on that surface; negative inverts it.

fill_surface.description: Rubber and seal: put the dark or light surface colour in the file instead of leaving it transparent.

ink_amount.description: Rubber and seal: how dark a photo prints, 10 to 80%.

wear.description: Rubber and seal: gaps where the ink didn’t take, 0 (clean) to 80%.

tilt.description: A few degrees off straight, as if stamped by hand.

output_dir.description: Folder to save results in. Default: next to each original. Originals are never overwritten.

tools.name: make_stat_shot
tools.description: A milestone as a shareable image, like the site’s Stat Shot: a big number or short text (e.g. “10,000”), a label (“followers on X”), an optional tag, message, name, handle, date and profile photo. Layouts: big (the number as large as it fits), centre, profile (a card with your photo), chart (a line climbing to the top right), badge (the number in a ring), headline (the label as a large headline: a new job, a launch), board (each character on a flip tile). Backgrounds: plain, gradient, glow, grid, dots, rays, waves, confetti, or image. Sizes: square 1080×1080, portrait 1080×1350, portrait-34 1080×1440, story 1080×1920, landscape 1600×900. PNGs in ~/Downloads/one-design. On the Free plan each image carries a small “Made with one.design” credit in the bottom right corner, as on the site; Pro has none.

value.description: The number or big text, e.g. “10,000”, “10K” or “New role”.

label.description: What it counts, e.g. “followers on X”, or for headline “Designer at Acme”.

kicker.description: A small tag above it (empty for none).

message.description: An optional short message, e.g. “Thank you for being here.”

photo.description: A profile photo (optional); without one, the profile layout shows your initials.

layout.description: big, centre, profile, chart, badge, headline or board.

background_design.description: plain, gradient, glow, grid, dots, rays, waves, confetti, or image (needs background_image).

dim.description: How much of the background colour lies over your image (0 to 80%), so the words stay readable.

accent.description: Accent colour (tag, label, chart, ring), hex like #c9f26b.

font.description: Font for the number and headline: sans (Inter), serif (Instrument Serif) or mono (JetBrains Mono).

output_dir.description: Folder to save into. Default: ~/Downloads/one-design.

tools.name: plan_and_pricing
tools.description: The current plan, what Free and Pro include (tools, batch sizes, QR codes, Brand Libraries) and the price. Use it when someone asks what’s free, hits a limit, or asks about upgrading.

tools.name: buy_pro
tools.description: Starts checkout for One Design Pro (Lifetime, paid once) and opens it in the browser. Only when the person asks to buy or upgrade. If they are signed in (sign_in), the purchase goes on that account; if not, Stripe asks for an email and the account is made or found from it. Payment happens on Stripe’s page, never here.

open_in_browser.description: Open the checkout page in the default browser. Off: just return the link.

tools.name: sign_in
tools.description: Sends a 6-digit sign-in code to an email address, to unlock Pro here for someone who bought it. Then call verify_sign_in with the code. Accounts are optional; Free works without one.

email.description: The email used for one.design or at checkout.

tools.name: verify_sign_in
tools.description: Finishes signing in with the code from the email, then checks the account’s plan. The session is saved on this computer (~/.config/one-design).

tools.name: sign_out
tools.description: Forgets the saved sign-in on this computer. Back to Free here.

tools.name: manage_billing
tools.description: Opens Stripe’s billing page for the signed-in account: receipts, invoices, card, or cancelling a subscription.

tools.name: brand_library
tools.description: Reads the Brand Libraries synced to the signed-in one.design account: colours (name and HEX), fonts, logos. Use the colours in other tools (QR codes, watermarks, store shots, bento). save_logos writes the logos to a folder so other tools can use them.

library.description: A library name. Default: all of them.

save_logos.description: Save the logos (and fonts) as files.

output_dir.description: Where to save them. Default: ~/Downloads/one-design.

tools.name: list_tools
tools.description: Every tool on one.design: what it does, whether it’s Free or Pro, and which MCP tool does it here (or that it runs on the site).

tools.name: open_in_one_design
tools.description: Opens a tool on one.design in the browser. For the tools that run an AI model on the device and so only work on the site: Cutout (background removal), Blur Faces, Magic Eraser, Brand Guidelines. Works for any tool, and for the pricing, account and Brand Library pages.

tool.description: A tool id or name (e.g. cutout, "blur faces", brand-guidelines), or pricing, account, brand.

instructions:
One Design (one.design) is a set of everyday image and document tools for designers and small teams. This server runs them on the person's own computer: files are read and written locally and never uploaded.

How to work:
- Act on the files the person names. Folders mean the images in them. ~ is their home folder.
- Originals are never overwritten. Results go next to them (name-suffix.ext) or into a folder they choose; new things (QR codes, cards, PDFs) go to ~/Downloads/one-design. Tell them where things went.
- Prefer one tool call over many: tools take lists of files.
- For anything that runs an AI model in the browser (Cutout background removal, Blur Faces, Magic Eraser, Brand Guidelines), use open_in_one_design: those work on the site, still on the device.
- Ready-made jobs are offered as prompts (blog images, social post, client delivery, app store launch, brand kit, share privately and more). The guides and size presets are resources (one-design://…); read one-design://presets/sizes before picking sizes for a platform.

Plans (tell people plainly when it matters, never nag):
- Free: 5 files per batch, 1 QR code at a time, the Free tools, a small credit on Stat Shot images, no Brand Libraries.
- Pro: every tool, batches of up to 50, 50 QR codes at once, no credit, Brand Libraries. Lifetime £29.99 once (launch price, was £79.99).
- When a tool answers that it's Pro, or a batch was cut to 5, say so in a sentence and offer Pro once. If they want it, call buy_pro (it opens Stripe checkout in their browser; payment happens there). If they already bought it, call sign_in with their email, then verify_sign_in with the code from the email.
- plan_and_pricing explains the plans; manage_billing opens receipts and the card; can't afford it, they can write to hello@one.design.

Style: plain English, short, no jargon.
